saints.name: The Annunciation of the Lord
saints.title: Solemnity of the Lord
saints.shortBlurb: The angel Gabriel announced to the Virgin Mary that she would bear the Son of God, and at her “yes” the Word was made flesh…
biography: In the sixth month of Elizabeth's pregnancy, the Gospel of Luke recounts, the angel Gabriel was sent from God to Nazareth, to a virgin espoused to Joseph of the house of David whose name was Mary. Greeting her as full of grace, he announced that she would conceive by the Holy Spirit and bear a son, Jesus, the Son of the Most High.

At her consent — "Behold the handmaid of the Lord: be it done to me according to thy word" — the eternal Word was made flesh in her womb. The feast thus honors at once the mystery of the Incarnation and the faith and obedience of the Virgin whose fiat made way for it.

Kept on 25 March, nine months before Christmas, the feast is first certainly attested in a canon of the Council of Toledo in 656 as celebrated throughout the Church, and the Council in Trullo in 692 exempted it alone, with Sundays, from the Lenten ban on feasts. In England it was long kept as Lady Day.
saints.knownFor: The Incarnation of the Word — “and the Word was made flesh.”
